6403.full: Ἄσσος, -ου (also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ή Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: Act.20:13-14 (see: ἆσσον).† (AS)

6405.full: ἐγγύτερος, see: ἐγγύς. ἐγγύς, adv., [in LXX chiefly for קָרוֹב ;] near; __1. of place: Jhn.19:20, 42; as prep. with genitive (M, Pr., 99), Luk.19:11, Jhn.3:23 6:19, 23 11:18, 54, Act.1:12; with dative, Act.9:38 27:8; superl., ἔγγιστα, Mrk.6:36, WH, mg.; metaphorically, ֹοἱ ἐ., opposite to οἱ μακράν, Eph.2:17; ἐ. γίνεσθαι, Eph.2:13; ἐ. σου τὸ ῥῆμα, Rom.10:8 (LXX). __2. Of time: Mat.24:32 26:18, Mrk.13:28, 29 Luk.21:30, 31 Jhn.2:13 6:4 7:2 11:55, Rev.1:3 22:10; ὁ κύριος ἐ., Php.4:5; before ἐπὶ θύραις, Mat.24:33; compar., ἐγγύτερον (neut. of adj. -ος, used adverbially), Rom.13:11 (cf. R, txt.); as prep. with genitive, ἐ. κατάρας, Heb.6:8; ἀφανισμοῦ, Heb.8:13 (cf. Cremer, 223). † (AS)

6406.full: 1. to shut in, close gates, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. to shut or confine within : Pass., ἑρκέων ἐγκεκλῃμένος (for ἐντὸς ἑρκέων κεκλῃμένος); (Sophocles Tragicus); δόμοις ἐγκεκλῃμένος (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. generally to confine , γλῶσσαν ἐγκλῄσας (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. Mid. to shut oneself up in , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6410.full: ἐγκράτεια, -ας, ἡ (-ἐγκρατής), [in LXX: Sir.18:15, 30 4Ma.5:34 * ;] __1. prop., mastery, control. __2. (sc. ἑαθτοῦ) self-control: Act.24:25, Gal.5:23, 2Pe.1:6 (see DB, iv, 558b 695a; Page on Ac, l.with). † (AS)

s: suborned to lie in wait, lying in wait
6414.full: ἐνκάθετος (Rec. ἐγκ-), -αν (ἐγκαθίημι), [in LXX: Job.31:9 (אָרַב), Job.19:12 * ;] suborned to lie in wait, lying in wait: as subst., Luk.20:20.† (AS)

s: to lay hands on, attack, assail
6415.full: 1. to put one's hand in or to a thing, to attempt it, with dative rei, (Euripides); with infinitive, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.: absolute to make an attempt or beginning , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to lay hands on, attack, assail , τινι (Thucydides) (ML)

6416.full: 1. to put into one's hands, entrust , τί or τινά τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: —;Pass., ἐγχειρίζεσθαί τι to be entrusted with a thing, (Lucian) 2. Mid. to take in hand, encounter , κινδύνους (Thucydides) (ML)

6418.full: to be long about a thing, to delay , (Thucydides):—;Pass. to become chronic , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to pour in wine, to fill the cup
6419.full: 1. to pour in , μέθυ ἐγχ. δεπάεσσι (Odyssey by Homer); οἶνον ἐς κύλικα (Herdotus Historicus); ἐγχεῖν alone, to pour in wine, to fill the cup , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.: —;Mid. to fill one's cup , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. of dry things, to pour in, shoot in , (Odyssey by Homer) 3. with accusative of the cup, to fill by pouring in , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. ἐγχεῖν ὕδωρ τινί, i. e. to fill the κλεψύδρα (q. see.), (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

6420.full: ἐθίζω, [in LXX: Sir.23:9, 13 2Ma.14:30 ;] to accustom: pass. pf. ptcp., τὸ εἰθισμένον, the established custom, Luk.2:27.† (AS)

s: a jettison, a throwing overboard of cargo
6421.lxx: in LXX: Exo.11:1 (גָּרַשׁ), Jos.1:5 (ἐκβολὴν ποιεῖσθαι, טול hi.), Eze.47:8 (יָצָא)*
6421.full: ἐκ-βολή, -ῆς (ἐκβάλλω), [in LXX: Exo.11:1 (גָּרַשׁ), Jos.1:5 (ἐκβολὴν ποιεῖσθαι, טול hi.), Eze.47:8 (יָצָא)* ;] __1. a throwing out. __2. a jettison, a throwing overboard of cargo: Act.27:18 (cf. Jos, l.with; and see Field, Notes, 144 f.).† (AS)

6422.full: to throw out foam, of the sea:—;Pass., of ships, to be cast ashore , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to bind a thing to oneself, hang it round one
6425.full: to bind so as to hang from, to fasten to or on , with genitive, (Iliad by Homer): absolute, σανίδας ἐκδῆσαι to bind planks (to his back), (Odyssey by Homer):—;Mid. to bind a thing to oneself, hang it round one , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6426.full: 1. to call out or forth, summon forth , (Homer) 2. Mid. to call out to oneself , (Odyssey by Homer) 3. to call forth, elicit , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 4. with infinitive to call on one to do, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6427.full: ἐκ-κλάω, -ῶ [in LXX: Lev.1:17 (שָׁסַע pi.)* ;] to break off: pass., Rom.11:17-20.† (AS)

6431.full: 1. Dep. to compute, calculate , (Plutarch) 2. to consider, reflect on , τι (Herdotus Historicus); περί τινος (Thucydides) 3. to reckon on , οὐδεὶς αὑτοῦ θάνατον ἐκλογίζεται (Euripides) (ML)

s: to measure for oneself, take measure of
6432.full: to measure out, measure , χρόνον (Euripides):—;Mid. to measure for oneself, take measure of , τι (Xenophon Historicus); ἄστροις ἐκμετρούμενος χθόνα calculating its position by the stars, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6433.full: 1. to pillage , (Euripides), etc.:—;Pass., of a person, to be undone , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to carry off as plunder , (Thucydides) (ML)

6440.full: ἐμ-πλέκω [in LXX: Pro.28:18 (נָפַל), 2Ma.15:17 * ;] to weave in, entwine; pass., metaphorically, to be involved, entangled in: 2Ti.2:4, 2Pe.2:20.† (AS)

6442.lxx: in LXX: before εἰς, Num.12:14 A, Deu.25:9 (יָרָק)*
6442.full: ἐμ-πτύω [in LXX: before εἰς, Num.12:14 A, Deu.25:9 (יָרָק)* ;] = cl., καταπτύω (Ruth., NPhr., 66), to spit upon: with dative, Mrk.10:34 14:65 15:19; before εἰς, Mat.26:67 27:30. Pass., Luk.18:32.† (AS)

6443.lxx: in LXX: Deu.33:19 (סָפַן), Eze.27:3 (רָכַל); ἐ. εἶναι, Isa.23:17 (זָנָה)*
6443.full: ἐμπόριον, -ον, τό (ἔμπορος) [in LXX: Deu.33:19 (סָפַן), Eze.27:3 (רָכַל); ἐ. εἶναι, Isa.23:17 (זָנָה)* ;] a trading place, exchange: οἶκος ἐμπορίου, Jhn.2:16.† (AS)

6444.full: 1. to let a thing be seen in a mirror, (Plato Philosophus):—; to exhibit, display , (Plutarch), etc. 2. Pass., with future middle to be seen in a mirror, to be reflected , (Plato Philosophus) 3. to become visible , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6447.lxx: in LXX for חִבֻּק pi., Pro.6:10 24:33 *
6447.full: ἐν-αγκαλίζομαι (ἀγκάλη), [in LXX for חִבֻּק pi., Pro.6:10 24:33 * ;] to take into one's arms: Mrk.9:36 10:16.† (AS)

6450.full: έν-δέχομαι [in LXX: Psa.119:122 (עָרַב), 2Ma.11:18 * ;] __1. to admit, approve. __2. to be possible; impers., ἑνδέχεται, it is possible: with accusative and inf., Luk.13:33 (Cremer, 687).† (AS)

6457.full: taken to heart , μή σοι ἐνθύμιος ἔστω take not much thought for him, (Odyssey by Homer); ἐνθύμιόν οἱ ἐγένετο he had trouble of heart , (Herdotus Historicus); τί δ᾽ ἐστί σοι τοῦτ᾽ ἐνθύμιο; what is 't that weighs upon thy heart? (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐνθύμιον ποιεῖσθαί τι to have a scruple about it, (Thucydides) (ML)

s: to nod to, make a sign to
6458.full: ἐν-νεύω [in LXX: Pro.6:13 10:10 (קָרַץ), Sir.27:22 A * ;] to nod to, make a sign to: with dative of person(s), Luk.1:62.† (AS)

s: to hatch as in a nest
6459.full: 1. to hatch young in a place, (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. with accusative to hatch as in a nest , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6462.full: 1. to pour in while molten , μόλιβδον (Plutarch) 2. Pass., with perfect active ἐντέτηκα, 3. of feelings, to sink deep in , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of persons, to be absorbed by a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

s: a lying in wait, an ambush
6463.full: ἐν-έδρα, -ας, ἡ (ἕδρα, a seat), [in LXX: Jos.8:7-9, Psa.10:8 (אָרַב)* ;] a lying in wait, an ambush: Act.23:16 (Rec. ἔνεδρον, a form frequently in LXX), Act.25:8.† (AS)

s: to change, turn another way, move back and forward
6466.full: 1. to change utterly or completely, (Euripides):—;Mid., μηδὲν ἐξαλλάσσεται he sees no change take place , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. to withdraw from a place, with accusative, (Euripides) 3. ἐξαλλάσσειν τί τινος to remove from , with genitive, (Thucydides) 4. intransitive to change, turn another way, move back and forward , (Euripides); ποίαν ἐξαλλάξ; which other way shall I take? (Euripides); ἐξαλλάσσουσα χάρις unusual grace, (Euripides) (ML)

s: to endure to the end, see out
6467.full: 1. to draw out water:—;metaphorically to endure to the end, see out , Lat. exantlare, exhaurire, (Euripides) 2. metaphorically also to rob, plunder , (Lucian) (ML)

6468.lxx: in LXX: Exo.8:29 (הָתַל hi.), Da TH Sus 5:6*
6468.full: ἐξ -απατάω, -ῶ strengthened form of ἀπατάω, [in LXX: Exo.8:29 (הָתַל hi.), Da TH Sus 5:6* ;] to deceive: with accusative, Rom.7:11 Rom.16:18, 1Co.3:18, 2Co.11:3, 2Th.2:3; pass., 1Ti.2:14.† (AS)

6471.full: 1. occurs in (Homer):—; to drive out from , ἄντρου ἐξήλασε μῆλα (Odyssey by Homer); absolute to drive afield , of a shepherd, (Odyssey by Homer):—;especially to drive out or expel from a place, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. 2. to drive out horses or chariots, (Iliad by Homer): Mid. to drive out one's horses, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus); so, ἐξελαύνειν στρατόν to lead out an army, (Herdotus Historicus): hence 3. intransitive to march out , (Herdotus Historicus): to drive or ride out , (Thucydides) 4. to knock out , (Odyssey by Homer) 5. to beat out metals, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6472.full: 1. to unroll , (Euripides):metaphorically to unfold , Lat. explicare, (Euripides) 2. of any rapid motion, ἴχνος ἐξ. ποδός to evolve the mazy dance, (Euripides):—;hence intransitive to wheel about , (Plutarch) 3. as military term, = ἀναπτύσσειν, Lat. explicare, to extend the front by bringing up the rear men, to deploy , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to draw off , (Plutarch) (ML)

6474.full: 1. a searching out, search , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a finding out, invention , (Herdotus Historicus) from ἐξευρίσκω (ML)

s: even bring to a level with
to be a match for, to rival
6476.full: 1. to make equal or even bring to a level with , Lat. exaequare, τινά or τί τινι (Sophocles Tragicus):—; Mid. to make oneself equal , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;Pass. to be or become equal , τινι (Plato Philosophus), etc.; to be a match for, to rival , τινι (Thucydides) 2. to put on a level , τοὺς πολίτας (Aristophanes Comicus) 3. intransitive to be equal or like , μητρὶ δ᾽ οὐδὲν ἐξισοῖ acts in no way like a mother, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ. τοῖς ἄλλοις (Thucydides): so in Pass., (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6479.full: ἐξ-ορύσσω [in LXX: Pro.29:22; ὀφθαλμόν (-ούς), Jdg.16:21, 1Ki.11:2 (נָקַר)* ;] to dig out, dig up: στέγην, Mrk.2:4; metaphorically, ὀφοαλμούς (cf. LXX, ll with; Herod., viii, 116), Gal.4:15.† (AS)

6487.full: ἐπ-αιτέω, -ῶ, [in LXX: Psa_109:10 (H7592) Sir_40:28 * ;] __1. to ask besides. __2. to beg (as a mendicant; cf. MM, Exp., xiv): Luk.16:3 18:35 (Cremer, 74).† (AS)

6490.full: ἐπ-αν-όρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (ἐπανορθόω, to correct, restore; of. 2Ma.2:22) [in LXX: I Est.8:52, 1Ma.14:34 * ;] correction: of life, 2Ti.3:16 (cf. MM, Exp., xiv).† (AS)

s: to bring the whole force of
6494.full: to drive against, drive home , ἔγχος (Iliad by Homer); ἐπέρεισε δὲ ἶν᾽ ἀπέλεθρον put vast strength to it, (Homer):—; ἐπ. τὴν φάλαγγά τινι to bring the whole force of the phalanx against, (Plutarch):—;Mid., λαίφη προτόνοις ἐπερειδόμεναι staying their sails on ropes, (Euripides):—;Pass. to lean or bear upon , τινι (Aristophanes Comicus): absolute to resist with all one's force , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6495.full: 1. Dep. 2. to pray or make a vow to a deity, with dative, (Homer), etc.:—;with infinitive to pray to one that . . , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. :—;with accusative rei, to pray for , (Aeschulus Tragicus): also, with accusative cognate, ἐπ. λιτάς (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. to imprecate a curse upon , τί τινι (Aeschulus Tragicus); with infinitive, ἐπεύχομαι [ αὐτῷ] παθεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus): absolute to utter imprecations , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. to glory over , τινι (Iliad by Homer) 5. to boast that , with infinitive, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

s: to plot against, lay snares for
to form designs upon, aim at
6496.full: 1. to plan or contrive against , κακὸν πόλει (Tyrtaeus Elegiacus); θάνατόν τινι (Herdotus Historicus):—;with dative pers. only, to plot against, lay snares for , τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); τῷ πλήθει (Aristophanes Comicus);—;absolute, οὑπιβουλεύων the conspirer , (Sophocles Tragicus): —;with accusative rei only, to plan secretly, scheme, plot , τὸν ἔκπλουν (Thucydides) 2. with dative rei, to form designs upon, aim at , πρήγμασι μεγάλοισι (Herdotus Historicus); τυραννίδι (Plato Philosophus) 3. with infinitive to purpose or design to do, (Herdotus Historicus) 4. Pass., with future middle -εύσομαι: aor1 -εβουλεύθην:—; to have plots formed against one, to be the object of plots , (Thucydides) 5. of things, to be designed against , πρᾶγμα, ὃ τοῖς θεοῖς ἐπιβουλεύεται (Aristophanes Comicus); τὰ ἐπιβουλευόμενα plots , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6497.full: ἐπι-βοάω, -ῶ to cry out: Act.25:24 (Rec., for βοάω, which see).† (AS)

6498.full: 1. to laugh approvingly , Lat. arrideo, (Iliad by Homer), attic 2. = ἐπεγγελάω, (Lucian) (ML)

6499.full: ἐπι-γίνομαι (see: γίνομαι) [in LXX: Ep. Jer.47:1-7, 3Ma.2:6 * ;] to arrive, arise, come on: Act.28:13.† (AS)
